problem: Robots cannot read human floor plan maps: no existing method computes a navigation plan from a map image plus a goal text, and building SLAM/occupancy maps and labeling areas is labor-intensive.
motivation: Architectural floor plans are readily available in human environments, but parsing them requires understanding labels, ambiguous label-to-area association and geometry (room connectivity via doors). VLMs reason jointly over images and text, so the paper tests whether they can parse floor plans to produce door-level navigation plans.
key_idea: Manually clean and densely label a floor plan image (uniform walls, yellow uniquely-ID'd doors, duplicated room labels), then prompt a VLM (GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet) with the image and start/goal text to output a JSON plan of ApproachDoor/OpenDoor/GoThrough actions.
insight: Visual prompt design matters much more than the raw model: processed maps far outperform raw maps (e.g. GPT-4o Domain 2 0.84 vs 0.21), and dense labels significantly improve accuracy (t=10.72, p<0.0001 on original_map_1) because VLMs otherwise mis-assign door ownership to the nearest label. Failures come from reasoning about door ownership and room-connectivity topology, which worsens in larger maps (doubled maps, t=6.13) and multi-room tasks.
method: Visual simplification: remove dimensions, scale bars, window icons and furniture symbols from raw CVC-FP floor plans, keeping only the map.
Structural standardization: uniform wall thickness, doors recolored yellow, windows replaced with walls.
Dense labeling: duplicate room labels near doors, intersections and inside large or irregular rooms.
Consistency check: all rooms enclosed, unique IDs for rooms and doors, exported as high-res PNG.
Instruction-based prompt: text specifies start/goal, allowed actions, and asks the VLM to first list all door/room connections before planning.
Plan output: JSON sequence of ApproachDoor(x), OpenDoor(x), GoThrough(x) actions.
Robot execution: Lite3 quadruped localizes with AMCL directly on the grayscale floor plan, DWA + A* navigation; door opening by asking humans for help.

setting.observation: single floor plan image (manually preprocessed) plus text prompt with start/goal; real robot uses camera image of the plan
setting.action_space: symbolic door-level actions: ApproachDoor, OpenDoor, GoThrough
setting.simulator: none (offline plan-correctness evaluation on floor plan images; real robot demo)
setting.privileged: manual map enhancement (wall thickening, door coloring, dense labels, door IDs); start and goal room names given

numbers_note: Map-size, difficulty and label-density results (including the headline 0.96 success on Map 1 hard tasks, and 135/150 GPT-4o trials on Domain 3) are only in figures or text, not tables. Table 'processed' values are sparse-label maps.
results: GPT-4o reaches up to 0.96 success on nine-action plans and 135/150 successful hard-task trials with dense labels on one domain (132 optimal). Processed maps strongly beat raw maps (e.g. 0.84 vs 0.21). On three campus plans GPT-4o hard tasks reach 0.80-0.94, above Claude (0.54-0.90) in most cases.
limitations: Map enhancement (thickening walls, removing annotations, dense labels, door IDs) is done manually
Accuracy drops on larger maps, multi-room tasks and sparsely labeled/open areas; VLMs confuse door ownership and connectivity
Small evaluation (3+3 maps, 50 trials each), robot must face the map at close range, and doors are opened by humans
